descriptionChirho: The ordinal numeral 'sixth,' indicating position in a sequence, used for days, months, years, sons, captains, and other ordered lists. The multilingual glosses are consistently ordinal: eng 'the sixth / sixth', spa 'el sexto / la sexta / sexto', arb السَّادِسُ / السَّادِسَةَ (al-sadisu/al-sadisata, masc/fem), hin छठवें / छठवीं / छठा (chhaTven/chhaTviin/chhaTa), kor 그 여섯째 / 여섯째 / 그 여섯 번째, swa wa sita / ya sita / ha sita. Both masculine and feminine forms across S144238, S144241, and S144244 express ordinal position.

A fractional quantity meaning one-sixth of a whole, used in Ezekiel for measurements of offerings (hin, ephah). Distinguished from the ordinal by the partitive construct: eng 'sixth of', spa 'sexta parte de' (explicitly adding 'parte'), arb سُدْسَ / سُدْسُ (sudsa, the specific Arabic fractional noun distinct from the ordinal سَادِس), hin छठवाँ भाग (chhaTvaan bhaag, 'sixth portion'), kor 육분의 일 (yukbun-ui il, 'one of six parts'), swa sehemu ya sita ya ('portion of sixth of'). The Arabic and Korean forms especially confirm a genuine fractional sense.
